A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ZEUS research. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable matching across additions, relocation, and renumbering.

before.justification: V1 reports original clustering, calibration, runtime, and regularization experiments on OpenML and synthetic datasets, with detailed appendix results.

after.justification: V2 retains those original empirical results and adds baseline comparisons, prior ablations, robustness tests, architectural experiments, and special-case evaluations.

M1.justification: Appendix G.4 adds a ZEUS+TabICL variant that substitutes the transformer backbone within the existing unsupervised pipeline. The default ZEUS architecture, synthetic prior, losses, and inference procedure remain unchanged; Section 3.1's additional architectural explanations are disclosures rather than demonstrated revisions.

E1.justification: The same 34 OpenML and two sets of 20 synthetic datasets are retained. Appendix G adds noisy and outlier-contaminated inputs plus four constructed scenarios: Cluster-Imbalance, Covariance-Scaled, Moons, and Connection. This extends test conditions within the existing clustering task.

E2.justification: Tables 1–2 and Appendix F.1 add IDC and k-means on TabPFN-Unsupervised and SCARF embeddings, substantially broadening comparison beyond the previous classical and autoencoder-based methods. Existing comparators remain; the calibration table and runtime figure retain their original comparator sets.

E3.justification: New experiments introduce controlled prior combinations, token dimensions of 32/128/512/768, and clustering-backend comparisons using the same checkpoint. Appendix G also specifies Gaussian noise with standard deviation 0.05 and 5% injected anomalies, evaluating the latter only on original points. These substantially expand evaluation design while retaining the main benchmark's preprocessing, metrics, and sample limits.

E4.justification: The original loss-component ablation is retained. Section 3.5 and Appendix F.4 add prior-component ablations, while Appendix G investigates noise/outlier robustness, token-size sensitivity, output clustering, backbone substitution, and challenging cluster geometries. These address several previously untested design choices and failure conditions.

E5.justification: Both versions report five-seed averaging for the main ARI and Brier comparisons. V2 adds no uncertainty intervals, dispersion estimates, formal significance tests, or explicit increases in repeated runs. Its noise standard deviation describes an experimental perturbation, not uncertainty in reported results.

E6.justification: V2 adds extensive baseline, prior-ablation, robustness, architecture, and special-case results. For example, Table 25 reports Moons ARI of 98.80 for ZEUS, 48.67 for k-means, and 49.23 for GMM. Original ZEUS aggregate ARIs remain 57.43/89.03/86.33, and the original Brier and regularization results are retained. Revised rank summaries reflect the expanded comparator pool rather than a same-setting performance decline.

T1.justification: Appendix B.1 introduces Theorem 1 and a three-step proof claiming componentwise approximation of arbitrary mixture distributions through neural transformations of Gaussian mixtures. V1 contains the PFN/Bayesian connection but no corresponding theorem. Section 2.2 now invokes this result to support synthetic-to-real generalization.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the central claims: fully unsupervised zero-shot tabular embeddings, no target-dataset fine-tuning, competitive clustering, and fast inference. The added experiments do not redefine these headline contributions.

C2.justification: V2 adds interpretations concerning complementary prior components, categorical-data sensitivity, robustness, and possible prior overfitting at larger token dimensions or with TabICL. It also explains the suitability of k-means and acknowledges that systematic investigation of genuine failure cases remains open. Section 2.2 adds a broader generalization assurance based on the new theorem.

D1.justification: Section 3.1 clarifies the absence of label embeddings, a query set, and an additional MLP decoder. Appendix E adds baseline repositories and specifies averaging TabPFN's per-column embeddings and following SCARF's example procedure; Appendix G provides new experiment recipes. Section 3.3 also drops v1's explicit 'without regularization' qualifier without documenting a calibration rerun.

R1.justification: V2 adds citations to SCARF, the OpenML platform review, TabICL, and Attention Is All You Need. These support added comparisons, implementation choices, and background; the overall positioning as PFN-inspired unsupervised tabular representation learning remains stable.

P1.justification: V2 makes localized language corrections, updates author affiliations/contact information and publication status, and expands architectural and prior-generation explanations. It adds subsections for the new material and moves licensing from Appendix G to H, while largely preserving the existing narrative and section order.

P2.justification: The hard-clustering tables gain three comparator columns. New Table 5, Tables 18–20, and Tables 21–25 display prior ablations and supplementary experiments, substantially expanding the visual evidence. Appendix tables are redistributed and recaptioned, and Figure 3 is enlarged; the four original figures retain their substantive content.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially strengthens the empirical assessment by adding relevant representation-learning baselines and testing previously unsupported choices of prior, architecture, and clustering backend, alongside robustness and difficult cluster geometries. These experiments expose meaningful tradeoffs, including poorer real-data performance with larger tokens or TabICL. The gains outweigh a theoretical overreach: the new distribution-approximation argument does not establish Section 2.2's broad assurance of successful clustering on arbitrary real mixtures.
